newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lamassoure declines comment on French tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Lamassoure declines comment on French tax cuts.

text.p: Budget minister Alain Lamassoure on Wednesday said he could not comment on reports that income taxes would be cut by 20 billion francs in the 1997 budget.
"I cannot tell you because I do not know the number," he said in an interview on French television station LCI.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe has pledged a major overhaul of the tax system over the next five years. The government now is putting the finishing touches on tax reforms to be presented to parliament in September along with the 1997 budget.
But Lamassoure poured cold water on a call by former conservative prime minister Edouard Balladur earlier this week for massive tax cuts to boost France's flagging economy.
He said such a move would endanger the government's ability to cut the deficit to qualify for European monetary union and send the French franc into a tailspin.
Lamassoure reiterated that the government planned to hold 1997 spending at 1996 levels in the 1997 budget.

Some 6,000 to 7,000 jobs would be cut from the civil service payroll next year through attrition as part of the government's drive to cut spending. Asked about long-simmering speculation that President Jacques Chirac might decide to replace Juppe, Lamassoure said Chirac always spoke highly of Juppe and the government at cabinet meetings.
